Proof: endpoint guards leave first.param < p < last.param. Let j be the first later index with point[j].param >= p. Then point[j-1].param < p <= point[j].param, so the earliest matching pair has distinct increasing endpoints. Distinct finite D64 endpoints have a nonzero exact difference of magnitude at least the least subnormal; rounded subtraction cannot become zero. It may overflow and fail at den instead, but cannot reach division with zero den. Do not count a direct DIV(1,0) as this binding scenario.
